samples.title: Phân loại rác
samples.prompt: Develop a talk about sorting household waste. Use these ideas: practical benefits, possible difficulties, and ways to improve the experience. Then answer the follow-up questions.
requirementsVi: Lợi ích: more recyclable material can be collected separately.
Khó khăn: residents may stop sorting if collection is unreliable.
Cải thiện: provide simple labels and explain how each type of waste is collected.
samples.summaryVi: Phân loại cần thùng và hướng dẫn rõ, đồng thời hệ thống thu gom phải thực hiện đúng.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: I would like to talk about sorting household waste. In my opinion, this topic is worth considering because it can affect ordinary decisions and experiences. I will look at a practical benefit, a possible difficulty and a way to make the approach work better.
paragraphs.noteVi: Giới thiệu chủ đề và ba nhánh sẽ triển khai.

paragraphs.label: Ý 1 — lợi ích thực tế
paragraphs.text: First, more recyclable material can be collected separately. This is possible because clear containers reduce the chance that paper and plastic become mixed with food waste. For example, a family can keep a small box for clean bottles instead of putting them in the same bag as dinner leftovers. That example shows how an idea can be useful in a real situation. People are more likely to value an approach when they can see what it changes in their own lives.
paragraphs.noteVi: Phân loại cần thùng và hướng dẫn rõ, đồng thời hệ thống thu gom phải thực hiện đúng.

paragraphs.label: Ý 2 — khó khăn
paragraphs.text: However, residents may stop sorting if collection is unreliable. One reason is that extra effort feels pointless when separated bags are later mixed together. For instance, a careful resident may see all bins emptied into one truck and decide not to separate waste again. I do not think this means we should reject the whole idea. It means that we need to understand the needs of the people involved before expecting the same result for everyone.
paragraphs.noteVi: Một trở ngại → lý do → ví dụ; tránh khẳng định tuyệt đối.

paragraphs.label: Ý 3 — cách cải thiện
paragraphs.text: A useful step would be to provide simple labels and explain how each type of waste is collected. To be more specific, a building manager could place picture labels above bins and publish a reliable collection schedule. I would start with a small trial and ask the people involved what helped and what remained difficult. Their feedback could then guide the next step, so that effort goes towards a real need.
paragraphs.noteVi: Giải pháp cụ thể → cách thực hiện → phản hồi.

paragraphs.label: Kết bài
paragraphs.text: To sum up, I think the potential benefit is valuable, but practical planning matters. We should keep the useful parts, recognise the difficulties and make changes when necessary. That would be more helpful than assuming that one approach suits everybody.
paragraphs.noteVi: Chốt quan điểm, không thêm luận điểm mới.

questions.question: Should everyone follow the same approach to sorting household waste?
questions.answer: No, I do not think so. People have different needs and resources. For example, a careful resident may see all bins emptied into one truck and decide not to separate waste again. A flexible approach would give that person a better chance to benefit.
questions.noteVi: Quan điểm → khác biệt nhu cầu → ví dụ.

questions.question: Who should help address the difficulty you mentioned?
questions.answer: The people organising the activity should listen to those taking part. They could provide simple labels and explain how each type of waste is collected. Participants should also explain what is difficult instead of assuming that organisers already know.
questions.noteVi: Nêu vai trò của cả người tổ chức và người tham gia.

questions.question: How could we tell whether a new approach is successful?
questions.answer: We could ask whether it solves the original problem and makes daily life easier. Here, we would want to see whether more recyclable material can be collected separately. I would compare people's experiences before and after a small trial rather than judge success by popularity alone.
questions.noteVi: Tiêu chí đo → áp dụng chủ đề → cách so sánh.

samples.prompt: Develop a talk about responsible wildlife tourism. Use these ideas: practical benefits, possible difficulties, and ways to improve the experience. Then answer the follow-up questions.
requirementsVi: Lợi ích: visitors can enjoy nature without treating animals as objects for entertainment.
Khó khăn: visitors may not know which activities are responsible.
Cải thiện: provide clear information about visitor behaviour and animal care.
samples.summaryVi: Tham quan thiên nhiên cần quan sát có khoảng cách; nên hỏi cách chăm sóc động vật thay vì chỉ xem quảng cáo.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: I would like to talk about responsible wildlife tourism. In my opinion, this topic is worth considering because it can affect ordinary decisions and experiences. I will look at a practical benefit, a possible difficulty and a way to make the approach work better.

paragraphs.label: Ý 1 — lợi ích thực tế
paragraphs.text: First, visitors can enjoy nature without treating animals as objects for entertainment. This is possible because keeping a suitable distance allows people to observe behaviour with less interference. For example, a guided birdwatching group can use binoculars instead of approaching a nesting area. That example shows how an idea can be useful in a real situation. People are more likely to value an approach when they can see what it changes in their own lives.
paragraphs.noteVi: Tham quan thiên nhiên cần quan sát có khoảng cách; nên hỏi cách chăm sóc động vật thay vì chỉ xem quảng cáo.

paragraphs.label: Ý 2 — khó khăn
paragraphs.text: However, visitors may not know which activities are responsible. One reason is that promotional photographs do not always explain how animals are treated. For instance, a tourist may book a close-contact experience because an advertisement describes it as educational. I do not think this means we should reject the whole idea. It means that we need to understand the needs of the people involved before expecting the same result for everyone.
paragraphs.noteVi: Một trở ngại → lý do → ví dụ; tránh khẳng định tuyệt đối.

paragraphs.label: Ý 3 — cách cải thiện
paragraphs.text: A useful step would be to provide clear information about visitor behaviour and animal care. To be more specific, a tour guide could explain why touching and feeding wildlife are not included and offer observation from a suitable distance. paragraphs.label: Ý 1 — lợi ích thực tế
paragraphs.text: First, people can avoid wasting treated water. This is possible because noticing leaks and unnecessary running taps can reduce waste without removing essential uses. For example, a household can repair a dripping tap and use a bowl when washing a small amount of produce. That example shows how an idea can be useful in a real situation. People are more likely to value an approach when they can see what it changes in their own lives.
